text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH

- Conservative opposition leader Tansu Ciller gave her support to religious high-schools facing the threat of partial closure under a compulsory eight-year schooling plan being introduced by the new secularist government.
- A military court has returned files on allegations that Ciller worked for US intellengence to the civilian state security court.
MILLIYET

- Four policemen accused of beating to death a leftist journalist did not turn up at court for the trial despite an order for them to attend from Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz. The court ordered the arrest of the men.
- The Istanbul gold exchange will begin to issue Turkish made gold ingots.
HURRIYET
- Five leading non-governmental organisation warned the government not to raise prices after a recent 32 percent hike on petroleum products which was reflected throughout the economy.
- An Islamist deputy resigned from his party on Thursday.
YENI YUZYIL
- Shop owners in the Laleli district of Istanbul, a centre for the so-called suitcase trade, have formed a union after a recent downturn in business.
RADIKAL
- The religious affairs directorate is at odds with a religious foundation over the division of 23 trillion lira raised by this year's Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca.
CUMHURIYET
- The military-dominated National Security Council meets in Istanbul on Friday. The council is expected to discuss Islamist business activities which earn around $15 billion annually.
DUNYA
- The government will decide on the offical minimum wage on July 29.
ZAMAN
- Parents who do not comply with the proposed eight-year compulsory education plan could be imprisoned for two months.
